newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-PIENAAR LEADS TRANSVAAL TO CURRIE CUP FINAL.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-PIENAAR LEADS TRANSVAAL TO CURRIE CUP FINAL.

text.p: Ousted Springbok captain Francois Pienaar was carried shoulder high from the field at Loftus Versfeld on Saturday after helping Transvaal reach next week's Currie Cup final against Natal.

Transvaal defeated arch-rivals Northern Transvaal 31-21 in the semifinal at the end of an extraordinary week for Pienaar, who was not part of the 36-man Springbok tour squad announced by manager Andre Markgraaff last Saturday.

An emotional Pienaar, asked if he would still be available for the Springboks if further injuries occurred, left the door ajar. "That's a tough question to answer at this stage. Obviously I have a contract with the South African Rugby Football Union and I must do what they say."

Monday is the deadline for players to prove their fitness for the tour of Argentina, France and Wales. Os du Randt and Christiaan Scholtz have already withdrawn and further casualties could yet bring Pienaar back from the brink.

On the field, Transvaal stunned Northerns with three tries in the first 48 minutes. Fullback Gavin Lawless opened the try scoring with a brilliant score in the right corner and Pienaar was prominent in the move which saw Springbok centre Japie Mulder force himslf over the line.

When another World Cup Springbok Rudolf Straeuli finished a movement which spanned the length of the field, Transvaal led 25-6 and despite a Northerns revival in the final quarter it was too little too late.
Natal, who have set the standard in South African rugby during 1996, earlier posted their 14th successive win in the competition by beating Free state 35-20.

Although former French international Thierry Lacroix and Springbok fullback Andre Joubert missed six kicks between them, Gary Teichmann's side ran in five tries through James Small, Federico Mendez, Wickus van Heerden, Joubert and Kevin Putt.
